title: Shanghai Biren Projects Up to 22-Fold H1 2026 Revenue Surge as AI Chip Demand Booms
detail: Shanghai Biren Technology, the Chinese GPU designer that listed in Hong Kong in January 2026, told the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on August 17 that it expects first-half 2026 revenue of 1.15 billion to 1.30 billion yuan (roughly $170.8M–$193.1M), up 1,852%–2,107% year-on-year, SCMP and TipRanks reported. The company projected a net loss of 320 million to 400 million yuan, narrowing 75%–80% from a year earlier, with adjusted loss narrowing 35%–47% to 290–360 million yuan. Biren attributed the surge to the domestic AI industry boom driving GPGPU demand, accelerated commercialization of its BIRENSUPA product line, and a more diversified customer base, while noting the low base in H1 2025 amplified the year-on-year growth rate. The filing lands amid a wave of similar guidance from second-tier Chinese AI chip designers — including Cambricon and Hygon — as US export restrictions continue to funnel domestic AI compute demand toward homegrown suppliers, pushing several toward the edge of profitability for the first time.

media.caption: Shanghai Biren Technology told the Hong Kong Stock Exchange it expects H1 2026 revenue up as much as 22-fold year-on-year, driven by surging domestic AI chip demand
